author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing opens at the first page when asked for a page below the first
summary: Asking the owner listing for a page below the first opens it at the first page and lists the matches, instead of showing the error page.
acceptance_criteria: given a search matching more than one owner, when the listing is asked for page zero, then the first page of matches is listed
given a search matching more than one owner, when the listing is asked for a negative page, then the first page of matches is listed
given a page below the first, when the listing is asked for it, then the reader sees the listing and not the error page
given an empty search listing every owner, when it is asked for a page below the first, then the first page of owners is listed
non_goals: page values above the last page
page values that are not a number
the veterinarian directory's handling of the same page value
notes: Recorded as REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 in docs/prd.md under Owner records, with edge cases 4 and 5. Non-Goals table untouched, so no scope_overrides. Two adjacent boundaries the owner did not decide are parked in Open Questions rather than assumed.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Durable memory handles this unchanged; no doc writes. The failure originates in OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName (line 135), not in the search itself: PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) throws IllegalArgumentException for any page below 1, which propagates to the error page. The PRD's file target is correct. The fix is a missing boundary check at a boundary the design already names: security-principles.md Trust Boundaries, row 'External input arrives' — validate range before use. Clamping a bound query parameter is request adaptation, which architecture-principles.md's pattern catalog places in the Web controller row; it is not a business rule, so the standing controller-business-rule deviation (system-design.md Package Structure) is not widened. No new type, package, or pattern; system-design.md Contracts and Constants stay accurate as written.
integration_points: processFindForm passes the same page value to findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and to addPaginationModel; both must see the clamped value
addPaginationModel publishes currentPage, from which ownersList.html derives every pagination link and the current-page highlight (lines 35-56)

patterns.description: the bound page parameter enters at processFindForm — normalize once there, before the query and before the model, rather than inside the paging helper
existing MockMvc listing tests give the shape for the two new cases; MockMvc is the project's one sanctioned mock

risks.risk: Clamping only inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName returns HTTP 200 with a first page of results while currentPage stays 0 or negative, so the template renders links such as /owners?page=-1 and highlights no page. That passes the acceptance criteria as written and still ships broken navigation.
risks.mitigation: Clamp at the entry of processFindForm so the same normalized value reaches both the repository query and addPaginationModel.

risks.risk: A page above the last currently falls into the isEmpty branch and reports 'not found'. That is an explicit non-goal of this slice; a clamp written as a general range fix could change it.
risks.mitigation: Clamp the lower bound only; leave the empty-page path untouched and add no test asserting the upper-bound behavior.

risks.risk: VetController:61 carries the identical PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) defect. Extracting a shared paging helper would reach into the veterinarian directory, which the prd-entry names a non-goal, and would collapse the two independently declared page sizes recorded in system-design.md Constants.
risks.mitigation: Fix OwnerController only. Leave VetController and the two page-size declarations as they are.

notes: Basis for the covered claim: grep over src/main/java for PageRequest.of resolves exactly two call sites (OwnerController:135, VetController:61) — no IDE oracle connected on this run, so this is the weaker text-match basis rather than a symbol resolution. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. No Known Defects row is added to system-design.md: that table lists defects that remain in the code, and this one is being fixed in this slice. Non-numeric page values stay outside scope — the int binding failure path is untouched.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: Clamp is normalized once at the entry of processFindForm and the same pageToShow value flows to both the repository query and addPaginationModel, avoiding the currentPage/query-mismatch risk the design-block flagged
Named constant FIRST_PAGE replaces a magic literal and documents intent
Fix scope stays confined to OwnerController; VetController's identical PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) defect is correctly left untouched per the design-block's recorded non-goal

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain not verified against the NVD this pass: no OWASP dependency-check plugin is configured in build.gradle (plugins are java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management, graalvm native, cyclonedx, javaformat) and this reviewer has no network access. The change set adds no dependency, so the surface is unchanged, but the NVD match for Spring Boot 4.1.0 and its managed Jackson remains a CI/human check, not a check that ran here. The committed CycloneDX SBOM task is the natural place to hang it.

Residual, unclamped upper bound (pre-existing, not introduced): `page` above the last page and very large values still pass through, producing a large database offset per request. Reachability is low - the query is bounded to pageSize 5 and Spring Data widens the offset to long - so this is a cheap-request-expensive-query nuisance, not a demonstrated DoS. The PRD already records it as the open question 'What should the owner listing do with a page above the last one, or with a page value that is not a number?'; closing that question is the right place to decide a ceiling.

Pattern divergence worth noting (scoped out by the PRD, not a defect here): VetController.showVetList takes the same @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page and calls PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) at VetController.java:61 with no clamp, so the two listings now normalize the same boundary input two different ways. The PRD's open question 'Does the veterinarian directory owe the same page rule as the owner listing?' owns this; if the answer is yes, the clamp belongs in one shared place rather than copied.
approved_aspects: Boundary validation strengthened: the request-derived `page` is clamped with Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) before it reaches PageRequest.of(page - 1, size), removing the IllegalArgumentException path that a page <= 0 previously took. Under the baseline that exception reached the error page, which system-design.md records as rendering the underlying exception message - so the change narrows an information-disclosure surface rather than widening one.

No new trust boundary: no new endpoint, route, or request parameter is introduced; /owners already accepted `page`. Exposed surface is unchanged (security-principles.md 'Widening the exposed surface' row does not fire).

No injection surface touched: the search value still flows only into the Spring Data derived query findByLastNameStartingWith via a bound parameter; no string-concatenated query text, no new value reaching a template, no change to output escaping.
No file, process, deserialization, reflection, or network operation added; no Runtime/ProcessBuilder, no Files/FileWriter, no XML/YAML/Jackson configuration touched.
No secrets: the diff adds no token, password, key, URL, or connection string; the only new constant is FIRST_PAGE = 1.
No concurrency risk: the controller stays stateless - pageToShow is a method-local int on a singleton bean, adding no shared mutable state.

No integer-overflow path introduced by the clamp: Math.max cannot overflow, and PageRequest.getOffset() widens to long before multiplying, so a large page yields a large offset rather than a wrapped one.
Tests exercise the boundary through the real MVC binding and dispatch (MockMvc), covering page=0, page=-1, and the empty-search variant - the three request shapes the new clamp governs.
No dependency change: build.gradle is untouched by the change set, so the supply-chain surface is unchanged.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owner listing page parameter to the first page

blast_radius.note: One module and one production method: OwnerController.processFindForm gains a FIRST_PAGE constant and a local pageToShow, 8 added and 2 removed production lines; the rest is one test file and two docs files, no sensitive paths, no build or config surface.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do exactly what the description says: pageToShow = Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) computed once at method entry and threaded to both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, so query and pagination links cannot diverge; the isEmpty, single-match redirect, and upper-bound paths are untouched, and the only follow-on is that a below-first page with exactly one match now redirects to the owner detail instead of the error page, which is the intended clamp behavior.

test_adequacy.note: Two @ParameterizedTest methods drive real MockMvc dispatch over page=0 and page=-1 for both the named and the empty search, asserting HTTP 200, the ownersList view, and currentPage=1; clamping in only one of the two consumers would fail one of those assertions, so the tests are not tautological, though the Pageable reaching the repository is matched with any() and the exact queried page index is never pinned.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four roster reviewers approved with empty findings, but the security reviewer's round-2 approval carries a recommendations list: VetController.showVetList (line 61) still calls PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) on the same unclamped @RequestParam, so the identical defect remains live in the sibling listing, the upper bound on page stays unclamped, and the supply chain was not checked against the NVD this pass.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, consultations, and design revisions; the diff matches the prd-entry's two file targets exactly, VetController is left untouched per the design-block's recorded non-goal, and the two docs edits are the PRD requirement entry and the one Contracts row the doc-reviewer demanded, with a stale open-question count corrected in passing.

rationale: The clamp itself is a textbook one-line boundary fix, read and confirmed in the hunks, with real boundary tests. Look before merging only at the security reviewer's parked note: VetController carries the identical unclamped PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) and still renders the error page.
